                    ### Question
                    It evaluates a patient with pelvic pain in which the simple Rx shows osteolytic and osteosclerotic lesions in the iliac and femoral bones. Point out the INCORRECT response.

                    ### Options
                    opa. I would request a bone map including skull and rib cage.
opb. I would request a determination of bone alkaline phosphatase.
opc. I would start estrogen hormone therapy.
opd. Endovenous bisphosphonates such as pamidronate and zoledronate are an effective option in this problem.

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
Pelvic pain with osteolytic and osteosclerotic lesions suggests possible underlying malignancy or metabolic bone disease. Requesting a bone map including the skull and rib cage is appropriate to identify lesions in other areas, aligning with the consensus that imaging can help in diagnosis. Determining bone alkaline phosphatase is relevant as it serves as a marker for bone metabolism, indicating elevated bone turnover. However, starting estrogen hormone therapy is inappropriate as it is typically used for osteoporosis and not indicated for osteolytic or osteosclerotic lesions. Endovenous bisphosphonates like pamidronate and zoledronate are used for certain bone conditions, but their effectiveness in this specific case is unclear, as they may not be the best option for all types of lesions. Therefore, the incorrect response is starting estrogen hormone therapy.
